content: Cefotaxime is an antibiotic used to treat a wide range of bacterial infections. It may also be administered to prevent infections associated with certain surgical procedures. This medication belongs to the cephalosporin class of antibiotics. Cefotaxime is administered via injection into a muscle or vein, as directed by a healthcare provider. When injected into a vein, the medication should be infused slowly over at least three minutes to minimize the risk of serious side effects, such as irregular heart rhythms. If you are using this medication at home, ensure you have been thoroughly instructed by your healthcare provider on its preparation and administration. Before use, inspect the solution for particles or discoloration; do not use it if either is present. If using a frozen pre-mixed solution, thaw the bag at room temperature or in the refrigerator. If thawed in the refrigerator, allow it to sit at room temperature for at least one hour before use. Do not thaw the solution using a water bath or microwave. After thawing, shake the bag well and check for leaks by squeezing it. Discard the solution if the bag leaks. For optimal effectiveness, cefotaxime should be used at evenly spaced intervals. It is crucial to complete the full prescribed course of treatment, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Stopping the medication prematurely may allow the infection to return. Common side effects include swelling, redness, or pain at the injection site. These effects are usually mild and temporary. However, this medication may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition known as Clostridioides difficile-associated diarrhea, which can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of cefotaxime may lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare but may occur. Symptoms of an allergic reaction include rash, itching, swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, and difficulty breathing. If you experience any of these symptoms, seek immediate medical attention. Before using cefotaxime, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, other cephalosporins, or penicillins, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other problems. Additionally, cefotaxime may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Cefotaxime passes into breast milk in small amounts and is unlikely to harm a nursing infant. However, consult your doctor before breastfeeding while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine glucose tests, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call emergency services immediately (911 in the U.S.). Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. While using cefotaxime, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as complete blood counts and kidney function tests, should be performed to monitor your progress and check for side effects. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about cefotaxime. It does not guarantee that this product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
